basics.name: Michael Johnson
basics.label: Lead Engineer
basics.summary: Lead engineer with nine years of experience building cloud-first, event-driven systems on AWS with .NET and consumer-facing web applications in Angular and React. Currently manages nine developers and production support for a healthcare navigation product serving millions of users. Background spans healthcare, benefits, energy, e-commerce, and media.

work.name: Alight
work.summary: Healthcare Navigation product connecting millions of users with providers, specialists, insurance guidance, and live agents.

highlights.text: Manage a team of nine onshore and offshore developers, the only engineers supporting the production Healthcare Navigation product, which connects millions of users with providers, specialists, insurance guidance, and live agents.

Own hundreds of repositories on a .NET, Java, AWS, SQL, and Angular stack with an event-driven architecture, making architectural decisions for new features and reworking layers that fail under load into scalable designs, while writing code 20–50% of the time.

Serve as the sole 24/7 on-call engineer under a zero-outage policy; led many major incidents and reduced production incidents by 87.3% through quality gates, improved code design, and clearing the ticket backlog.
Introduced code reviews with a "desk check" in which developers demo the happy path, expected failure conditions, and regression tests and explain the change.
Release daily or biweekly depending on change-management requirements; hire and onboard developers.
Designed cloud-first, event-driven inventory management systems on AWS Lambda, .NET, and SQL Server, using machine learning to match inventory items across multiple CRMs.
Migrated AWS Lambda applications to .NET 8 with Native AOT compilation, cutting cold-start times by up to 86% versus JIT-compiled .NET.
Built a consumer-facing Angular web application that lets users create items and record sets of matching items.
Managed relationships with client and consultant development teams delivering healthcare applications.
Designed and built .NET Core 3 and .NET 6 microservices to replace legacy monolith functionality, using event-driven designs to improve scalability and lower cloud costs.
Implemented a data warehousing solution for DynamoDB data, using Rockset for storage and an AWS-hosted .NET microservice to deliver admin-level reporting at low cost.
Established company-wide code quality standards, naming conventions, and a Git strategy with required PR reviews, static code analysis, and pipeline build checks.
Built a consumer-facing Angular web application that lets users create challenges and track health metrics.
Integrated user device health tracking in .NET 6 to automatically track health goals for participating users.

Built .NET Core 3 microservices for a natural gas pipeline: a FluentValidation service enforcing post-Enron regulations on whether each transfer is legal and feasible, and a traffic-flow service that identifies valid transfer times for orders.

Built React web applications with custom design libraries for an automotive seller (online car buying and selling; Sass, Tailwind) and a regional healthcare provider (static builds and CMS tooling that let copywriters publish without deployments).
Collaborated with directors on client technical proposals, including architecture diagrams and tech stack recommendations, and mentored junior engineers.
